compared) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused, exactly as a merge

You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A transfer to a sheet that already has a person with the same name or alias (as names are
compared) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused, exactly as a merge
does (claims after theirs, aliases joined, bound figures lost); the other sheet writes
PERSON_TRANSFERRED name=<name> from=<sheet id> then PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Transferring a person to a sheet that already has someone with the same name or alias now merges them into that person instead of being refused. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

**What happens on a merge** (in `TransferPerson.java`):
- The existing person on the other sheet is found by name or alias, compared the same way names are everywhere else.
- The arriving claims are copied in and listed after that person's own. They take the other sheet's next numbers and lose any figures a statement had bound.
- The arriving person's name and aliases become extra aliases of the person they merge into. Their grades, terms and contact are dropped, as an ordinary merge does.
- The other sheet's audit file gets `PERSON_TRANSFERRED … name=<name> from=<sheet id>`, then `PERSON_MERGED … from=<name> into=<name>`, then its usual rollup lines. The sheet they left still writes its `PERSON_TRANSFERRED … to=` record.

A new `People.transferInto` method adds the names to the existing person. It doesn't create a temporary person on the other sheet that would then be merged away. I also updated the one-line comment in `transfer.POST.yml`. The front end needed no change.

**Choices the request didn't cover:**
- **Still refused:**
  - the person being merged into is retired, matching an ordinary merge;
  - the arriving names match more than one person on the other sheet;
  - a name or alias is in use on another sheet in the other sheet's tree.
- **Contact:** the "contact already on the other sheet" refusal now only applies to a plain transfer. A merge drops the contact, so it can't clash.
